title: NUPEA: Optimizing Critical Loads on Spatial Dataflow Architectures via Non-Uniform Processing-Element Access
problem: On large spatial dataflow architectures (SDAs) where program instructions are distributed across a fabric of processing elements (PEs), some PEs are physically closer to memory than others, creating non-uniform data access latencies (NUPEA). Existing approaches focused on NUMA-style data placement, which is complex and often ineffective when critical data is hard to identify statically.
motivation: Data movement is the dominant energy, performance, and scalability bottleneck in modern architectures, and SDAs provide a new opportunity to reduce it by placing critical load instructions (rather than data) near memory, which is easier for compilers to reason about.
method: NUPEA observes that on large SDAs, placing critical load instructions on PEs physically close to memory reduces data movement costs. The authors implement architecture extensions and compiler optimizations for NUPEA on the Monaco SDA (by Efficient Computer) and its effcc compiler. The compiler identifies critical loads via dependence analysis and maps them to near-memory PEs, while the architecture exposes PE-to-memory proximity information to the compiler. This contrasts with NUMA where data is moved closer to fixed PEs.
key_novelty: NUPEA inverts the data-centric NUMA paradigm: rather than moving data near compute, it places compute (load instructions) near memory on spatial dataflow architectures, which is more tractable for compiler analysis.
contributions: Formalization of the NUPEA concept and contrast with NUMA-style data-centric approaches on SDAs
Architecture and compiler optimizations for NUPEA implemented on the Monaco SDA and effcc compiler
28% average speedup over a uniform-PE-access SDA across a range of important kernels
20% average speedup over a UPEA SDA augmented with NUMA

metrics.speedup: 28% avg over uniform-PE-access SDA; 20% avg over UPEA+NUMA SDA

limitations: Evaluation is limited to the Monaco SDA platform; generalizability to other spatial architectures is not systematically assessed.
primary_theme: instruction placement near memory on spatial dataflow architectures
